routines.name: Lead collector
routines.does: Reads 131 agency, vendor and news feeds in several languages every 30 minutes, plus any the source scout has added, and files new items as leads.

routines.name: Vulnerability feeds
routines.does: Syncs CISA's known-exploited catalog and EPSS and CVSS scores; re-rates affected events; refreshes the internet-disruption and disaster-alert map layers.

routines.name: CVE history
routines.does: Superseded by the CVE corpus (cve.yml). Kept every CVE NVD has published in a compact searchable database on the cve-data branch, reading only what NVD changed each day; the site copies it in when it deploys.

routines.name: CVE corpus
routines.does: Keeps every published CVE current from the official CVE List (with CISA's enrichment), EPSS daily and CISA's known-exploited dates, for the CVE lookup page; files new notable CVEs (exploited, known exploited or CVSS 9+) as leads for the research loop.

routines.name: Live site monitor
routines.does: Checks the live site, its security policy and data freshness; browser check twice a day.

routines.name: Open-source collectors
routines.does: Asks three independent news indexes in 12 languages, the EU and US vulnerability databases, Have I Been Pwned, leak-site tracking, Hacker News and the own status pages of 46 cloud, CDN, DNS, SaaS, payment and telecom providers (config/status-pages.json; major or long incidents only), so no single search engine decides what is seen.

routines.name: GDELT knowledge graph files
routines.does: Reads GDELT's 15-minute Global Knowledge Graph files (English sources and 65 machine-translated languages) once each, keeps articles GDELT tags as cyber attacks, hackers or cyber crime whose headline reads as cyber, and files each as a lead with the publisher's own page, its language and the country it names first. Runs every research cycle; collect.yml is the backup.

routines.name: Breach notification registers
routines.does: Runs with the open-source collectors and asks each official breach register at most hourly (California, Washington and Iowa attorneys general, the UK ICO's enforcement actions, and SEC 8-K Item 1.05 filings once a contact address is set): every new notice is a lead from a government source, read by a researcher who cites the regulator's own page.

routines.name: Power grid outages
routines.does: Runs in the research loop every few minutes (collect.yml every 30 minutes as backup): reads grid operators' public outage feeds and open grid data, tracks incidents from start to end, finds outages unusual for the hour and what corroborates them, gathers outages reported in the news, and audits every source each cycle (failing or frozen feeds, sudden falls, misplaced points). Map context, never cyber events.

routines.name: Vendor security advisories
routines.does: Reads twelve vendors' own security advisories as structured data (Microsoft, Cisco, Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian, Oracle, Google Chrome, Apple, Mozilla, Ivanti; CSAF where the vendor publishes it): severity and fixed versions as the vendor states them, and the vendor's own exploited statement, joined to every CVE on the Vulnerabilities page. A vendor's exploited statement or a critical advisory for widely used software becomes a lead for the research loop, never an event.

routines.name: Exploit watch
routines.does: Checks GitHub for public repositories naming each exploited flaw and flags them in the workbench as possible exploit code.

routines.name: Industrial advisories
routines.does: Reads industrial control system (ICS/OT) advisories as structured data: CISA's ICS and ICS medical advisories and Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB and Phoenix Contact as CSAF documents, CERT@VDE, Moxa and Mitsubishi Electric from their RSS feeds; joins them with CISA's known-exploited catalog for the Vulnerabilities page's Industrial view, and files exploited or critical ones, and high-scoring ones in lifeline sectors, as leads for the research loop (scripts/ics.mjs, no AI model).

routines.name: Scam warnings
routines.does: Reads official scam and phishing warnings from government bodies, police, regulators and national CERTs in several countries and languages (config/scams.json), types them by a fixed keyword map, and lists them by country in the map page's Insights tab. Warnings, not cyber events; one that describes a cyber incident becomes a lead for the research loop.

routines.name: Lead triage
routines.does: Clears leads already on file, plain non-events and expired items, then groups everything into stories ranked by how many independent publishers report them.

routines.name: Link check
routines.does: Checks every source link from the last 30 days and lists the broken ones for the verify desk.

routines.name: Pipeline check
routines.does: Measures every stage of the pipeline against its limit, restarts a late stage's workflow, and checks the data itself: keys vanishing from status.json, duplicate events, events waiting over 2 hours for their second review, lead files and the data branch growing abnormally, failing feeds and collectors. Problems show under What needs attention; one that lasts opens a GitHub issue labelled pipeline-alert, closed when healthy.

routines.name: Weekly security check
routines.does: Static security check of the code and data, plus the live site's policy.

routines.name: Sweep
routines.does: Continuous research loop: every few minutes it collects leads, researches new stories and second-reviews earlier events in parallel, then commits (target: lead to published and reviewed in under 15 minutes). The four schedules restart it when it is not running.

routines.name: Review desk
routines.does: Catch-all for second review: a second agent re-reads the sources of every new or changed event and passes, corrects or flags it. Most reviews happen inside the research loop (continuous review); this desk takes whatever is left every 2 hours, up to 6 reviewers.

routines.name: Backlog desk
routines.does: Keeps the research queue empty when the research loop falls behind: rules close routine bulletins and commentary, triagers sort the remaining headlines, and up to four researchers take what the loop did not reach. Every 3 hours; the loop's own rules run at every collection.

routines.name: Verify
routines.does: The verify desk, twice a day: settles disputed events, finds a second independent source for single-source ones, answers readers' error reports, repairs quarantined records, broken or front-page sources and duplicates by rule, and notes open problems for the owner (it took over the data steward and the watchdog).

routines.name: Report review
routines.does: Reads original government and vendor reports and records findings and recommendations.

routines.name: Analysis
routines.does: Finds patterns, chains and ripple effects across the week, once a day before the morning brief.

routines.name: Deep sweep
routines.does: Regional, native-language research where coverage is thin.
routines.retired: 2026-11-20: 1 run (Opus routine, 3 workers, $1.07) added 1 event; two of three workers read no page. The daily regional desk and the loop's gap researchers (a region in depth every 30 minutes) hunt the same thin regions; the deep sweep's region groups and local-language duty moved into the regional desk's weekly rotation.

routines.name: Daily brief
routines.does: Writes the brief for defenders (morning in the Americas, morning in Asia) and records daily counts.

routines.name: Watchdog
routines.does: Triages alerts, late routines and error reports, and fixes what it can.
routines.retired: 2026-11-20: 1 run, found nothing (guard healthy, one stale fallback issue). Its checks duplicate the guardian (guard.mjs --heal every 2 hours, outside the ops session) and the verify desk (event reports); its small code fixes broke the rule that jobs never push code. Event reports and quarantined records: verify desk; stale data, late routines and failed deploys: guardian; status.health: verify desk.

routines.name: Security review
routines.does: Reviews the week's code changes and data for security problems.

routines.name: Triage desk
routines.does: Sorts what the rules cannot: leak-site claims (kept only for organisations of public importance) and stories that keep being passed over, which it queues first for the research loop. Every 6 hours; to be merged into the backlog desk once that run sorts claims itself.

routines.name: Regional desk
routines.does: One thin region a day (Africa, the Middle East, Turkey and Latin America most often), researched in its own languages from national CERTs, regulators and critical-infrastructure operators; it took over the twice-weekly deep sweep.

routines.name: Follow-up desk
routines.does: Runs inside the research loop every 2 hours (config/pipeline.json flow.followup_every_minutes): checks whether developing stories and claims were confirmed, denied or grew, and updates them. Its separate daily schedule was switched off on 2026-11-20.

routines.name: Outage desk
routines.does: Runs inside the research loop every cycle (config/pipeline.json flow.outage_workers): outage checkers verify outage reports nobody had checked (power outages reported in the news that no operator feed covers, country-level internet disruptions measured by IODA, major outages on providers' status pages) from the operator's, provider's or government's own page and credible reporting, and record confirmed, not confirmed or a cyber lead for the research loop (scripts/outage-desk.mjs). A confirmed internet or service outage can become an outage event with a second review; a power outage stays context. Off when usage is tight.

routines.name: Claims desk
routines.does: Runs inside the research loop every cycle (config/pipeline.json flow.claims_workers), also when usage is tight: claims checkers take ransomware and extortion leak-site claims nobody had checked, most notable victim first (critical sector, government, health, large companies, other reports naming the victim, the group's track record), and look for the organisation's own statement, a regulator filing or a government notice, then credible reporting (scripts/claims-desk.mjs). Confirmed by the victim becomes a confirmed event, reported by two publishers a claimed event (severity 1, hidden by default), both with a second review; denied, unconfirmed (checked again later) and not found are recorded. Leak sites are never cited or linked and stolen data is never described.

routines.name: Data steward
routines.does: Repairs weak or broken sources, long summaries and duplicates, by rule.
routines.retired: 2026-11-20: 2 runs: fixed 23 leak-site sources (front page to listing page) and merged 5 duplicate groups. Its build-warning step was already verify's step 6, and its link, redirect and duplicate repairs do not need a daily wake-up of their own: all of it moved to the verify desk under the same rules (docs/jobs.md, Verify, steps 5 and 6).

routines.name: Tabletop exercise
routines.does: Turns one real, verified event of the week into a ready-to-run team exercise: scenario, timed updates, questions and what good looks like.

routines.name: Advisory desk
routines.does: Reads the vendor's own advisory for each exploited flaw and writes the workbench's check, fix and detection steps.

routines.name: Exploit analyst
routines.does: Opus agents read the vendor advisory, CISA and researchers' write-ups for each flaw in the workbench and explain how it is exploited (never code) and the remediation path: fix, workarounds, verification, and what to do if compromised.

routines.name: Community moderator
routines.does: Checks every community post against fixed rules, then reviews it for harm and unsourced claims before it can appear; handles reports of published posts. The research loop checks for posts about every 25 minutes; this schedule is the backup every 3 hours.

routines.name: Source scout
routines.does: Repairs broken sources, retires noisy ones, and adds official feeds and local-language searches for the thinnest regions (Africa, the Middle East, Turkey, Latin America first) and for critical infrastructure.

routines.name: Editor
routines.does: Reviews the week's pipeline numbers and corrections, fixes the three biggest problems in configuration, and reports what needs code.
routines.retired: 2026-11-20: had not run yet (weekly, Opus); its duties overlap the daily improver (same metrics, same goal: tune the pipeline from evidence) and the scout (feeds and queries). Weekly review, instruction fixes and data/pipeline.json: improver on Saturdays; noisy feeds and queries: scout.

routines.name: Guardian
routines.does: An independent check, outside the session that runs the other jobs: confirms fresh, validated data is live, restarts what is overdue, and alerts the owner if it cannot.

routines.name: Improver
routines.does: Continuous improvement: reads the week's cost, yield, speed and second-review results and makes up to three small, bounded, logged changes to the pipeline's dials and per-role models; on Saturdays it also does the weekly editor's review (the three biggest problems, precise instruction fixes for recurring corrections, data/pipeline.json). Anything bigger goes to the owner as a request.
